uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast UK consumer prices are rising. The Bank of England targets it at 2%, so it moves rate expectations and the pound; the September figure also sets benefit uprating.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: Economists have put a number on the UK's exposure to a US diesel ban: inflation of 5% if it goes ahead. This September reading shows how far prices had run before any such shock, and it sets the baseline any diesel effect would be measured against.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-10.recent: September brought 3.7% inflation on gasoline and just 29,000 new jobs against 90,000 expected, leaving Warsh's committee split between officials who want another hike by year-end and a labor market that has stalled. It meets as Trump's panel weighs removing Governor Lisa Cook from its ranks.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, nearly double the target, and with business activity at a 3½-year high, Wunsch says the ECB will probably have to hike again after last month's move. The complication is France: Moulin says it needs no ECB help yet, and the bar for the crisis tool is now argued over in public.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-10.recent: Three sources say the Bank of Japan may declare that underlying inflation has hit its 2% goal. Yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, so the meeting turns on whether rising prices have become domestic and durable or remain a weak currency passing through.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: Bank of England officials have divided in public over the inflation risk facing the UK, which makes this meeting a test of which reading carries the committee. The vote count will show how wide that divide runs, and the decision sets the cost of borrowing for UK households and firms.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: Gasoline lifted September prices 3.7% over the year, while the Labor Department counted just 29,000 new jobs against 90,000 expected, so the two halves of the mandate are pulling apart. Officials are split over another hike by year-end, and Trump has convened a panel to remove Governor Lisa Cook, one of the votes at the table.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The US presidency has pushed to return the G20 to its original priorities, and Russia's sherpa has said Moscow backs that push. The summit settles how much of the agenda the group still carries, and how far it narrows toward the economic core it began with.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Euro-zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, nearly double the target, even after that month's hike. Knot and Wunsch have both since argued for tightening again. Governments have until 28 October to name Isabel Schnabel's successor, and Moulin says France needs no ECB rescue yet.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: Bank of England officials have split in public over how large the inflation risk facing the UK is, so this decision arrives with the committee's disagreement already on the record. The vote count settles which reading of that risk prevails, and how far apart its members remain.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Three sources say the Bank of Japan may declare that underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal, a finding that would change the case for raising rates. Yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, so the December meeting weighs whether that pressure is domestic and lasting or carried in through the currency.
